title: The National Supercomputing Internet AI community reported public Kimi K3 API and model-download access after release
source_unit: National Supercomputing Internet AI community Kimi K3 service announcement as reported by 36Kr
geography: China, National Supercomputing Internet AI community, Kimi K3, enterprise and developer API users

observations.period: July 28, 2026; the day Kimi K3 open weights became available

denominator.unit: public Kimi K3 service route reported as launched by the National Supercomputing Internet AI community

service_status.value: API calling service and model-file download/deployment route reported as online

access_mode.value: enterprise and developer users could call through an API and download model files for deployment

interface_compatibility.value: not disclosed in the 36Kr service flash
interface_compatibility.unit: OpenAI/Anthropic compatibility not coded from this source

observations.method: Review of a 36Kr news flash reporting the National Supercomputing Internet AI community's service launch. The record codes public service availability as a platform-level endpoint and deliberately does not infer Hygon-specific execution, demand, or adoption from the announcement.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not identify the service operator's exact compute pool, model-serving site, accelerator mix, API price, capacity, service-level performance, customer identities, or post-launch usage. It reports access availability rather than verified successful customer workloads.
observations.subgroup: Chinese enterprises, developers, AI application builders, public-compute platform operators, domestic model providers, and accelerator vendors
observations.counterinterpretation: A one-click API route can lower setup friction while remaining capacity-constrained, costly, or lightly used. Public availability can coexist with continued private-cloud and foreign-accelerator use; it does not prove broad diffusion or state-directed substitution.

related_sources.claim: Moonshot's official Kimi release page states that Kimi K3 weights and technical materials were opened on July 27, 2026.
Hygon's official report describes domestic DCU model adaptation, but does not identify the National Supercomputing Internet service's accelerator allocation.

boundary: This record establishes a reported public API/model-access endpoint for Kimi K3. It does not establish Hygon-specific utilization, actual customer workloads, request volume, service reliability, revenue, public procurement, market share, or accelerator substitution.
